**First touch: p2 · `domain:ui` · `pm:queue`.** Not a queue jump: no menu entry opens the unfiltered Packages page, so turning off a code-loaded module needs a typed URL. This is an admin navigation detail (#25098 ruling 甲 context).

repo:hotcrm#2 · os-mickey · session_01ASNY8XiE8ZJYbrmzFDtS9g

Correction to this card's reading · 2026-11-18T17:55Z

A second hotcrm dev measured the console on 18.6.0 in objectstack-ai/hotcrm PR #2667, at hotcrm head `12ae2dde`, with Playwright and an admin user. They reached Studio without typing a URL: console home → **New in Studio** opens `/_console/studio` (the App Builder) on a *New Package* form; **Cancel** shows Studio's package list, and that list includes **HotCRM Revenue**. So "no Studio app is served" in the body is true only of the address `/_console/apps/studio`. Studio itself is served at `/_console/studio`, and it has a menu door from home.

What this does **not** settle: whether Studio's package list (or a package's page in it) offers **Disable** / **Enable** for a code-loaded module, which is the unfiltered Packages door `setup-nav.contributions.ts` promises. The #2648 dev read the App Builder's package pillars (Data, Automations, Interfaces, Access, All metadata) and found no Disable. Triage should re-read the defect as "Studio is reachable from home, but no menu door leads to the page that disables a module" before grading. The click path above is the starting point.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbP6iSEGkWb5fn8yqd

Browser readings B1–B3 before any code · 2026-11-19T12:17Z

Tree: objectstack `origin/main` 43639a6f, packages and Console built from that tree. Boot: `examples/app-multi-package` under `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin` on a private port, fresh SQLite. Its module `com.example.multi.orders` (type `module`, depends on the app `com.example.multi.core`, Source: Code) is served `disableable: true`. Playwright (Chromium), admin user, 1400×900.

**B1 · click path: works end to end.**

| Step | Visible | Reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Home → "New in Studio" | yes | lands on `/_console/studio` with the New Package dialog open |
| Cancel | yes | the Studio landing; both packages are listed as cards under "Installed apps" |
| Open the module's card | yes | `/_console/studio/com.example.multi.orders/data` |
| Top-bar package chip ("Multi-Package Orders · Read-only") | yes | opens the switcher popover |
| Popover foot entry | yes | it is labelled **"Package info & settings"**, not "Manage" (the key `engine.studio.pkg.manage`) |
| The detail sheet | yes | Type `module`, Scope "Read-only · code", Status Enabled; actions View info · Disable · Export |
| Disable → confirm | yes | `PATCH /api/v1/packages/com.example.multi.orders/disable` → 200; sheet shows Status Disabled and an Enable button |

**B2 · after the disable: Enable is reachable.** A fresh load of `/_console/studio` still lists the disabled module's card (with no sign that it is disabled). Opening it reaches its Data pillar, the chip and the same popover entry are there, and the sheet offers **Enable**: `PATCH …/enable` → 200; `GET /api/v1/packages` reads it back as enabled. So a disabled package is not stranded.

**B3 · the Studio landing offers neither door.** Landing cards carry only the name button and Customize, both of which open the package's Data pillar. Buttons matching manage / info & settings: 0. Links to the unfiltered `component/developer/packages` route: 0.

**Reading of the premise.** "No menu disables a code-loaded module" does not hold on this boot: the door exists, three clicks deep, under a label that names neither Disable nor Manage. What holds is the analysis's narrower defect: the landing gives no direct door to the sheet and no link to the full package list. Proceeding with route ② and ③ as dispatched; B2 shows no Enable gap, so ② carries no must-fix beyond the landing door.
